modules.name: minisvc.config
modules.purpose: Defines immutable runtime settings and loads database path/read-only configuration from an environment mapping.

modules.name: minisvc.models
modules.purpose: Defines the Order data model used between the API and repository.

modules.name: minisvc.storage.repo
modules.purpose: Persists and retrieves orders in SQLite and initializes the orders table.

modules.name: minisvc.audit
modules.purpose: Builds order audit-event dictionaries; it does not persist them.

modules.name: minisvc.api.handlers
modules.purpose: Implements create and read order application handlers.

modules.name: minisvc.api.routes
modules.purpose: Registers HTTP POST and GET routes and binds them to handlers.

modules.name: minisvc.cli
modules.purpose: CLI bootstrap: loads environment settings, constructs the repository, initializes SQLite schema, and reports readiness.

key_functions.description: Maps MINISVC_DB (default orders.sqlite) and MINISVC_READONLY == 1 into Settings.
Creates the orders table if absent.
Inserts an Order into SQLite using parameterized SQL.
Looks up one order and reconstructs an Order, or returns None.
Builds an Order from required payload keys, converts total_cents to int, saves it, and returns a created response with an in-memory event.
Reads an order and returns either missing or an order response with an in-memory read event.
Constructs a dict containing order type, action, order_id, and total_cents; no database write occurs.
Binds POST /orders and GET /orders/<order_id> via lambdas capturing the repository.
Bootstraps configuration and SQLite schema, prints readiness, and returns zero.

runtime_flows.name: CLI startup
steps: pyproject.toml dispatches the minisvc command to minisvc.cli:main.
load_settings selects MINISVC_DB or orders.sqlite and records readonly from MINISVC_READONLY.
main constructs OrderRepository with the selected path.
main calls init_schema, which creates orders if needed using SQLite.
main prints readiness and returns 0; readonly is not enforced by this flow.

runtime_flows.name: HTTP create-order
steps: The app dispatches POST /orders to a lambda registered in routes.py.
create_order reads order_id, customer, and total_cents and converts total_cents with int().
create_order calls OrderRepository.save, which inserts the order into SQLite.
create_order calls audit.order_event to build an in-memory created event and returns the response; no audit table write occurs.
